title: Redwood cost econ discovery - Olympus Capital
summary: Discovery focused on unit economics for embeddings/chat use cases; discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, per-token pricing, batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, and a strict monthly budget target. Agreed to send pricing worksheet, security docs, and run a short benchmark with 10k sample prompts.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sarah Kim (Olympus - Head of Data), Devon Brooks (Olympus - Engineer), Marcus Lee (Olympus - CTO)
Recording id: ff-20260304-olympus-0001

Summary auto-gen: cost-focused discovery; customer has strict monthly budget, evaluating hosted vs dedicated; wants benchmarking and pricing worksheet.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Sarah Kim: Hi Lena, Sarah here.
[00:08] Devon Brooks: Devon here.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: Marcus on the call.
[00:12] Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood, SE. I can jump into the cost models and benchmarking stuff.
[00:16] Lena Park: Great. High-level goal for today is to understand cost per unit for our chat and embedding workloads, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the right fit given your budget.

[02:05] Sarah Kim: To give context: we're doing doc ingestion for due diligence and an assistant for analysts. Two main workloads: embeddings for search (batch ingest + real-time vector updates) and chat completions used in our analyst UI. We have a monthly budget cap of roughly $12k for inference starting next quarter.
[02:27] Marcus Lee: And security wise, we may need VPC peering and KMS integration if we go private. But first thing is cost 
d we can't exceed that budget.

[04:10] Marco Diaz: Understood. Can I ask expected QPS and token distribution? Even rough percentages help tune batching.
[04:18] Devon Brooks: For chat: typical request is 200-350 tokens in prompt+expected 100-200 tokens generation. Peak QPS is about 10-12 during analyst hours, average maybe 2-3. For embeddings: initial batch ingest is 1.2M docs over a month, steady-state near 30k embeddings/day.

[06:30] Lena Park: Cool. So rough cost drivers: per-token generation for hosted and dedicated differs; batching and KV/prefix caching for chat can reduce per-token cost noticeably; quantized models reduce GPU cost on Dedicated/Private. We'll walk through examples.

[08:01] Marco Diaz: Quick note: our hosted per-token price for a mid-size chat model is X (redwood uses $/1k-token metric internally), and the Dedicated cost is expressed as $/GPU-hour + model throughput. For a workload like yours, the economics often shift at predictable usage thresholds 
d we'll show the math.

[08:34] Sarah Kim: Can you walk through a sample calc? Say 5k chat requests/day avg, 300 tokens total each.

[09:00] Marco Diaz: Sure. Live calc 
d hosted example: assume 300 tokens * 5000 = 1.5M tokens/day, times 30 = ~45M tokens/month. At hosted rate of $X per 1k tokens 
d substitute X in worksheet 
d that would be about $Y/month. But with batching and caching we can reduce tokens and per-token compute because repeated prefixes can hit KV cache, and we can reduce generation length with system prompts.
[09:25] Devon Brooks: Sorry can you spell KV cache? I saw it as "KV cash" in a deck earlier.
[09:29] Marco Diaz: KV cache, K-V like key-value 
d it's the transformer cache so if you reuse prefixes we don't re-compute them and it cuts computation.

[11:02] Lena Park: For embeddings, hosted is pretty straightforward per-vector cost. If you do dedicated, you can run batched embedding jobs on GPU for lower $/embedding but you need reserved capacity planning to meet peak ingest windows.

[12:45] Marcus Lee: We're a bit fuzzy on the break-even point between hosted and dedicated. At what monthly token count does dedicated become cheaper?

[13:05] Marco Diaz: Typical break-even for chat-heavy workloads is often in the 20-100M tokens/month band depending on model class and latency SLO. For embeddings, tens of millions of vectors or frequent high-throughput batch jobs push you to dedicated. But specifics depend on model (FP16 vs 8-bit quant), batchability, and whether you can tolerate slightly higher tail latency in exchange for lower unit cost.

[15:20] Sarah Kim: Our constraint is budget $12k/month. If hosted comes in at $15k, that's a no-go. Are there levers to bring hosted under $12k without moving to Dedicated?

[15:45] Marco Diaz: A few levers: 1) prompt engineering to reduce token churn and system prompt size; 2) caching repeated user/context prefixes (KV cache) to avoid recomputation; 3) using model variants 
d smaller models for low-risk flows; 4) response length caps and reranking to avoid over-generation. Combined they can often reduce effective tokens by 20-40%.

[17:30] Devon Brooks: How does batching interact with latency? We can't have >200ms added to median latency for interactive analysts.

[17:42] Marco Diaz: Continuous batching groups requests that arrive within a short window (tens of ms) and maintains low added latency. For your QPS, we can configure the batch target to keep median latency within your SLO while increasing GPU utilization. If you need strict p99 latency, we may use a latency-first policy 
d that impacts cost.

[19:00] Lena Park: Also worth noting Redwood's smart routing 
d you can route non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants or to lower capacity pools during peaks. That reduces overall spend.

[21:12] Marcus Lee: Private/on-prem option: we'd pay more for setup and infra but get better control. Does private help cost-wise or mainly compliance?

[21:30] Marco Diaz: Private is primarily for compliance and data residency. Cost-wise, if you have existing on-prem GPU capacity and ops resources, it can be competitive. But include the ops overhead and KMS/HSM integration costs. Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity) often hits the sweet spot for predictable throughput without your ops lift.

[23:05] Sarah Kim: Any impact from quantization on output quality? We can't afford meaningfully degraded answer quality for analysis.

[23:20] Marco Diaz: Quantization to 8-bit or 4-bit is model-dependent. We recommend validating on your eval prompts. There is usually a small quality delta; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and run evals so you can see quality vs cost tradeoffs. We'll include recommended profiles in the worksheet.

[26:00] Devon Brooks: Can you show examples of how caching reduces compute?

[26:10] Marco Diaz: Example: if user prompts include a 150-token instruction prefix repeated across requests, with KV cache you only compute that prefix once and subsequent requests only compute new tokens. If prefix is 40% of tokens, you save 40% of compute. In practice we see 10-50% savings depending on UX.

[28:40] Lena Park: I'll point you to the pricing worksheet I'll send 
d it has templated scenarios: hosted baseline, hosted with 30% effective token reduction from caching+prompting, dedicated with reserved GPU-hours amortized, and private with ops costs.

[30:12] Marcus Lee: On Dedicated, how do we size reserved capacity? We have peaks to 12 QPS but only for 3 hours/day.

[30:25] Marco Diaz: You can configure burst and autoscaling; reserved capacity covers baseline throughput and you can have burst capacity billed at a marginal rate. For your peak pattern we might recommend a committed baseline sized for steady state and enable burst for the 3-hour peak, or schedule horizontal scaling for that window. We'll model both.

[33:50] Sarah Kim: Any hidden costs? Data egress, logs, evals?

[34:00] Lena Park: Good point. Hosted includes token invoices and basic logging within retention; advanced observability (longer retention, per-token cost breakdown) is an add-on. Private has networking/KMS costs on top. We'll put all of that in the worksheet line items.

[36:10] Devon Brooks: We'd like to run a benchmark. What do you need from us?

[36:20] Marco Diaz: Ideal: 10k representative prompts, distribution of token lengths, a small sample of embeddings workload. We'll provide a seed script to run locally or via our harness, and we'll return a benchmark report with cost projections for Hosted and Dedicated and recommended quantization.

[38:05] Sarah Kim: Timeline: we need numbers by next Tuesday to include in Q2 planning. Is that doable?

[38:20] Marco Diaz: We can kick off bench the moment you share prompts. Draft plan by 3/9, preliminary numbers by 3/12.

[40:00] Lena Park: Recap: we'll send pricing worksheet (Lena), SE benchmark plan + seed script (Marco), customer shares 10k prompts (Sarah). We'll model hosted baseline and hosted with caching/batching levers, plus a Dedicated sizing with reserved + burst scenario.

[41:10] Marcus Lee: One more question 
d does Redwood support KMS rotation and HSM for private deployments?

[41:22] Marco Diaz: Yes, private includes KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logs; we'll send the security pack. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and transit and SOC 2 docs; Private is for stricter requirements.

[44:45] Sarah Kim: Any recommended models? We want strong accuracy but cost matters; are there middle-ground models you recommend for embeddings and chat?

[45:00] Marco Diaz: For embeddings, mid-size open models often provide a good accuracy/cost tradeoff; for chat, a smaller fine-tuned variant for low-risk flows and a larger one for assistant-critical flows. We'll list model candidates in the worksheet and show cost delta.

[47:10] Devon Brooks: If we move to Dedicated and later to Private, how hard is migration?

[47:22] Lena Park: We provide the same API surface and rollout paths. Migration is mostly infra/provisioning and KMS/networking; our rollout tooling makes model versioning and canaries straightforward. We'll include a migration checklist.

[50:30] Marcus Lee: Ok that helps. Anything we should be aware of regarding SLA and uptime for Dedicated?

[50:40] Marco Diaz: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; specifics depend on the contract tier. We'll include standard SLA terms in the follow-up.

[52:05] Sarah Kim: Great. We'll get the prompts over by end of day Thursday.
[52:12] Lena Park: Perfect. We'll send the pricing worksheet and security pack after this call. Marco will follow up on the benchmark plan. Thanks everyone.
[54:58] End recording.
